content: The British Association for Immediate Care (BASICS) is a registered charity that serves as the national coordinating body for both organizations and individuals providing immediate care across the United Kingdom. The organization relies on volunteer medical professionals to deliver immediate healthcare assistance. BASICS is an association of healthcare professionals who undergo additional training to become immediate care practitioners. These members offer their services in support of statutory or voluntary ambulance services. The organization operates on four levels for its members: as a professional body representing their interests, as an operational body facilitating individual schemes, as a training body to enhance members' knowledge, and as an advisory body for members and other stakeholders. BASICS members are often called upon to provide advanced skills at the scene of major incidents or for particularly challenging patient cases. In such situations, individuals may be summoned on a case-by-case basis by the local ambulance control center. The importance of BASICS' work was highlighted during the July 7th terrorist attacks in London, after which the British Medical Association initiated a series of training courses over three years, organized by BASICS. Additionally, BASICS members frequently work at private events, often alongside voluntary ambulance services like the Red Cross and St. John Ambulance, or statutory services. These events include large sporting events (such as Football Association matches), major incidents, public rallies, mass gatherings, and concerts. At the local level, BASICS assists ambulance service trusts in situations requiring a multi-agency response or when additional skills and qualifications are necessary. For example, in an industrial accident where a worker is trapped in machinery, the ambulance service may collaborate with the fire service to coordinate the rescue. BASICS can enhance the skill set available at the scene by providing a medical doctor capable of performing procedures beyond the scope of paramedics, such as administering advanced analgesia or conducting necessary surgical interventions to extricate the patient. BASICS initially began as a small group of General Practitioners concerned about the immediate care provided to car crash victims. Their goal was to bring increased clinical expertise to the scene on a voluntary basis. Today, BASICS doctors come from a wide range of specialties, including General Practice, Surgery, Medicine, Emergency Medicine, and Anaesthesia & Critical Care. Registered nurses also play a critical role in pre-hospital care as part of BASICS. Their contributions vary widely, from acting as first responders delivering life-saving defibrillator shocks to functioning as immediate care practitioners at the Advanced Nurse Practitioner level. These advanced practitioners operate with significant clinical autonomy and decision-making capabilities, ensuring high-quality care for patients in urgent situations.
